output.title: Anonymise first, automate second
output.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, make one decision first: will any document that enters the process still contain customer identifiers? If yes, stop and strip or mask those details before you test AI on it. That applies to quotes, invoices, contracts, case notes, and neat-looking summary slides too. A workflow is only as tidy as the input you give it.

For an owner-operator, the useful check is simple. Pick one recurring workflow you already handle in email, CRM, a shared drive, or a Zapier/Make step. Then trace where the document first leaves your control and where human review still happens. If a step depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample first and use that as your test set. Keep the human review where the risk is highest.

This is not AI magic and not legal advice. It is a governance choice the owner makes before any build. Once the sample is clean, the next question is not “can we automate?” but “should this workflow be automated at all?”
